cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: the real coefficient of 6-9i
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes '=IMREAL("6-9i")' with the result 6. Exact and definitional: the real coefficient of x+yi is x. Note the result is a NUMBER, not one of the complex strings the rest of the IM* family returns -- IMREAL and IMAGINARY are the two extractors, and this corpus compares their results numerically rather than as text.

cases.description: A pure imaginary number, whose real coefficient is zero
cases.expected_note: Exact: 4i parses as 0+4i, so the real coefficient is 0. The mirror of the documented example, and the case that distinguishes "the real part is zero" from "there is no real part" -- the argument is written with no real term at all, exactly as the IM* format prints such numbers.

cases.description: The x+yj form the page also documents
cases.expected_note: The page's description says "in x + yi or x + yj text format", so the j suffix is documented. The real coefficient of 3+4j is 3 by the same definition.
